hypothesis: With hashed state each SLOAD runs keccak256(address) through the global keccak cache (lookup + bucket lock, part of keccak_cache's ~19% of heavy-phase server CPU in base-symbols) even though the 10k-slot call reads one account. Keeping the last (address, hash) pair on the provider drops one cache lookup per SLOAD. Expect ~3-5% off heavy (~2-3% total), light flat.
llm_commentary: Reusing the last (address, keccak) pair across storage reads (commit 96cdbe72d7) is a clear win on every family, with disjoint run ranges: c8a 5.11→5.00s (-2.2%), c8i 6.74→6.41s (-4.9%), c8g 8.06→7.51s (-6.8%), in line with the 2-3% total predicted on c8a and above it elsewhere. The 10k-slot heavy call reads one account, so this removes 10k global keccak-cache lookups per call (hash the input, find the bucket, take its lock, compare); Intel and Graviton gain more because the cache's bucket lock and the extra hashing cost more there than on Zen 5. Cumulatively the three commits are -6.7% on c8a, -10.6% on c8i and -15.6% on c8g against the bare baseline. The slot hash is the remaining keccak-cache lookup per SLOAD; next are the light phase (spawn_blocking handoff, 60% kernel time) and the compiler leftovers (znver5, PGO).
